notes: Rows: the first 32 rows of the test's Rows[64][4] table (Run() copies all 64, the 32-lane dispatch reads Rows[0..31]). Use exactly 32 rows = one wave32: columns 0..11 are wave-wide (v_readfirstlane, exec/vcc branches decided by all lanes), so extra rows or a second wave would change nothing in this wave but would add rows Expected32 does not have.

Words 5..32 are the kernel's own 0xdeadbeef sentinels for v10..v23; they are in the range, so no pre is needed. v24, v25 (columns 14, 15) are never written; the test checks only Checked=14 columns (0..13).

EXEC: six blocks 's_and_saveexec_b32 s14, vcc_lo ... s_or_b32 exec_lo, exec_lo, s14' restore EXEC to its entry value (full wave) before the next block; the body ends with full EXEC, so no post fix-up. All branches (execnz/execz/vccnz/vccz/cdbg*) jump forward 1..3 words inside the body.

Column 12 (cdbg_not_taken): s_cbranch_cdbgsys/cdbguser/cdbgsys_or_user/cdbgsys_and_user branch on the wave's conditional-debug bits, which only a debugger/trap handler sets; on a plain HSA dispatch without rocgdb they are 0, so none is taken and s12 = 0x1000+1+2+4+8, as on the PS5 without a debugger. If the oracle ever runs under a debugger this column is not comparable.

Column 13 (hints): s_setprio, s_inst_prefetch, s_clause, s_waitcnt_depctr, s_ttracedata (writes M0 to the thread-trace buffer only when tracing is enabled; no register effect) have no data effect; m0 is written (0x1234) but not reported.
Check() skips the 12 cross-lane columns on hosts with subgroups < 32; the oracle always runs a full wave32, so compare all 14.
verified: disassembly (llvm-mc gfx1030) of words 5..189 for Wave32Code: sentinel v_movs, 12 readfirstlane/v_cmp/branch blocks writing v10..v21, cdbg chain into v22, hint block into v23; every branch target inside [5,190]; Run()/Check() read (Checked=14, CrossLane flags).
